verses.english: 13. Another Chapter of Abbreviated Texts on the Ganges

verses.pali: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gaṅgā nadī pācīnaninnā pācīnapoṇā pācīnapabbhārā;
verses.english: “Mendicants, the Ganges river slants, slopes, and inclines to the east.

verses.pali: evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcindriyāni bhāvento pañcindriyāni bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro.
verses.english: In the same way, a mendicant developing and cultivating the five faculties slants, slopes, and inclines to extinguishment.

verses.pali: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcindriyāni bhāvento pañcindriyāni bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro?

Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddhindriyaṁ bhāveti rāgavinayapariyosānaṁ dosavinayapariyosānaṁ mohavinayapariyosānaṁ …pe… paññindriyaṁ bhāveti rāgavinayapariyosānaṁ dosavinayapariyosānaṁ mohavinayapariyosānaṁ.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant develops the faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom, which culminate in the removal of greed, hate, and delusion.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcindriyāni bhāvento pañcindriyāni bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro”ti.
verses.english: That’s how a mendicant developing and cultivating the five faculties slants, slopes, and inclines to extinguishment.”
Six on slanting to the east,
and six on slanting to the ocean;
and that’s how this chapter is recited.
